docRequirement: sub-agents.md § *Let subagents spawn their own subagents*: "By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation. At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork, so a subagent at the limit does its delegated work itself and returns one summary. A fork at the limit keeps `Agent` in its inherited tool list, but the tool returns an error instead of spawning." The limit is configurable: "To change the limit, set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to the number of subagent layers you want below your main conversation", "Set `1` to turn nesting off", and env-vars.md's row for that variable adds "(default: 3) … Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed." Per-agent opt-out is by definition, not by global default: "To keep one subagent from spawning while nesting is on … omit `Agent` from its `tools` list or add it to `disallowedTools`."
current: Nesting is off, hard-wired, at two independent layers, and there is no knob. (1) DEPTH BUDGET DEFAULT IS 1. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110` is `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1` (docblock :104-108 'ONE level of delegation'), and `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107` is `depth: 1` inside the frozen `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG` (mirror comment :104-106). The gate is `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:513-520`: `const depth = (args.depth ?? 0) + 1` then `if (depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)) return failure(args.agentDef.name, 'Subagent depth limit exceeded (' + ... + ')')`. (2) THE DEFAULT IS THE EFFECTIVE PRODUCTION VALUE. `maxDepth` reaches the spawner only through `maxDepth: config.orchestrator?.depth` (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1279`), and the single production seed builder — `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4152-4164` — writes only `contextSeed`, `sessionDepth`, `sessionIsFork`, `forkSubagent` and `tierModelMap`, never `depth`, so `normalizePiOrchestratorConfig` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:233-262`) falls back to `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth = 1` on every real session. A fourth literal repeats it: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4932` `maxDepth: parentBudgets?.maxDepth ?? 1` on the plugin-hook agent-admission spawn. (3) NO OVERRIDE EXISTS. A NUL-safe `grep -ral SPAWN_DEPTH .` returns only files under `docs/` — zero in `packages/`, `apps/` or `scripts/` — and there is no `NESSY_*DEPTH` reader either, so neither Claude's `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` nor a Nessy spelling is read anywhere. The only channel is `orchestrator.depth` on the execution manifest, which no production path sets. (4) A SECOND, INDEPENDENT LAYER ALSO BLOCKS NESTING. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:33-40` puts `'subagent'` in `ORCHESTRATION_TOOLS`, and :141 subtracts that whole set from the inherited pool of any descriptor that declares no `tools` — so a subagent without an explicit tools list never receives the `Agent` tool at ANY depth, unconditionally, not at the limit. The four builtin agents also lack it (`packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:157-158, 162-195` — `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`/`FULL_TOOLS` contain no `subagent`). The child's pool is then frozen: `allowedTools` (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:296-298`) copies `agentDef.tools` into `restrictions.tools`, which becomes the child session's `piAllowedTools` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:12163`). (5) THE REFUSAL SHAPE IS THE FORK SHAPE FOR EVERYONE. At the limit we return an error from the call (`spawner.ts:518-519`) rather than withholding `Agent`; the comment at :514-517 records the deviation knowingly. (6) Documented as 1: `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:47` — 'depth | 1 | … Default is ONE level of delegation'. Tests pin it: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.test.ts:531-534` ('defaults nesting depth to 1 in every place that defines a default'), :541-548 (grandchild refused), :550-555 (positive control: `maxDepth: 2` admits it), `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.test.ts:97`.
divergence: Two deltas, both on the same doc sentence, plus one absent knob. (a) VALUE: the nesting budget defaults to 1 where the page says 3. Depth 1 is precisely Claude's documented 'nesting off' setting, so we ship the off configuration as the default. Nothing about the mechanism, the field name (`orchestrator.depth` → `budgets.maxDepth`) or the enforcement point is wrong — only the number. (b) MISSING OVERRIDE: `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` has no reader and no Nessy-spelled equivalent, so the value cannot be changed by a user at all; the doc's `settings.json` `env` example has no effect. This half is not-built, not mis-valued. (c) WITHHOLDING RULE INVERTED IN SCOPE: the page withholds `Agent` from a subagent AT THE LIMIT; we subtract `subagent` from every tool-less subagent's inherited pool at every depth (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:141`) and, for an agent that names it explicitly, return `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)` at call time — which is the page's FORK behaviour applied to named subagents. At today's limit of 1 the two layers happen to agree; raising (a) alone would change nothing observable, because (c) still keeps `Agent` out of every default subagent's pool. That coupling is the reason this is one fix and not two.

userImpact: Observable, and it looks like a product limitation rather than a setting. A subagent cannot delegate at all today, on two surfaces. (1) The common case is silent: a user's or an imported plugin's agent that declares no `tools` list never receives the `Agent`/`subagent` tool, so a reviewer subagent asked to 'dispatch a verifier per finding' simply does the whole job itself in one context — the user sees a flatter, slower, more context-hungry run and no error explaining it. (2) The explicit case is a visible tool error: an author who lists `Agent` in the agent's `tools` gets `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)` back from the first delegation, mid-run, in the subagent's transcript. Either way there is no setting to change it — putting `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` in a settings `env` block (the exact remedy the page prescribes) does nothing, because nothing reads it. Users porting a Claude Code workflow that relies on nested delegation get a different result shape with no diagnostic.
